title: Further results on the smoothability of Cauchy hypersurfaces and Cauchy time functions
locators: Theorem 1.1 and Remark 4.14; §2 definitions of Cauchy hypersurface and acausal submanifold; Theorem 1.2 for smooth Cauchy temporal levels
relevance: Theorem 1.1 extends compact spacelike acausal embedded submanifolds with boundary to smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurfaces. Remark 4.14 allows disconnected acausal submanifolds componentwise. Theorem 1.2 supplies smooth Cauchy temporal levels. Used for the finite-point smooth screening necessity proof.
limits: Full text selectively audited: Theorem 1.1, Remark 4.14, §2 definitions, and Theorem 1.2. Does not prove extension of arbitrary noncompact acausal partial hypersurfaces; only the finite acausal point set is used.
assumptions: Smooth globally hyperbolic spacetime; compact spacelike acausal submanifold for Theorem 1.1; Cauchy temporal splitting hypotheses for Theorem 1.2.

title: Wave Equations on Lorentzian Manifolds and Quantization
locators: Corollary 3.2.4 (PDF pp. 76–79; arbitrary smooth homogeneous solution uniqueness from zero Cauchy data); Proposition 3.2.5 (PDF pp. 80–81; local Cauchy uniqueness); Theorem 3.2.11 (PDF pp. 85–87; global existence/uniqueness with compactly supported data, distinguished from the needed arbitrary-solution uniqueness)
relevance: Corollary 3.2.4 is the direct source for the fixed-background normally hyperbolic homogeneous uniqueness step; Proposition 3.2.5 supports its local-domain form.
limits: Full text selectively audited at the stated corollary/proposition/theorem locators. Application to an open partial surface K uses the standard geometric fact that D(K) is an open globally hyperbolic domain with K Cauchy. No coupled Einstein–matter uniqueness or cross-background comparison follows.
assumptions: Smooth globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold, smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface, smooth normally hyperbolic operator and smooth solution; zero field and normal derivative on the Cauchy surface.

title: On the Existence of a Maximal Cauchy Development for the Einstein Equations - a Dezornification
locators: Definition 2.1 and vacuum initial-data constraints (PDF p. 10); Theorem 2.7, Global uniqueness (PDF p. 11); Lemma 3.1 (isometric-immersion first-jet rigidity, PDF pp. 11–12); Corollary 3.2 (agreement from a Cauchy surface)
relevance: Theorem 2.7 gives a common GHD extension for two GHDs of the same vacuum initial data; Lemma 3.1 propagates equality of two isometric immersions from matching value and differential on a connected common source. These support the conditional finite-geodesic comparison after open-domain, connected-path, and first-jet hypotheses are verified.
limits: Full text selectively audited: Definition 2.1, Theorem 2.7, and Lemma 3.1. Vacuum Einstein theory only. The theorem does not by itself include coupled matter fields or establish the partial-domain geometry for every K; it does not imply equal lifetimes/whole-future isometry and does not require input GHDs to be maximal.
assumptions: Definition 2.1 requires a connected smooth d-dimensional Riemannian initial manifold with vacuum constraint data; no completeness requirement is stated. Theorem 2.7 applies to two smooth vacuum GHDs of the same data; embeddings preserve the initial data and time orientation.

title: Lorentzian causality theory
version: Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3; online text consulted 28 October 2026
locators: Theorem 4.123 (Avez–Seifert: globally hyperbolic spacetime, any distinct causally related pair is joined by a length-maximizing causal geodesic), with proof immediately following
relevance: Supports the optional strengthening's use of a causal geodesic from the mark to each distinct point of its causal future. For chronologically related endpoints the Lorentzian distance is positive, so a length-maximizing geodesic is timelike.
limits: Statement/proof checked as a standard theorem source, not as an original-source audit. Completeness from the marks is an additional hypothesis and is not implied by global hyperbolicity.
